A1.justification: Both PDFs are complete, readable 27-page versions of the same paper, Mixture of Parrots. Their text, equations, figures and appendices support a reliable comparison, including matching renumbered appendix content.

before.justification: Sections 4–5 and Appendix B report original phone-book and shortest-path experiments, pretrained model evaluations, and generalization-gap analyses.

after.justification: Sections 4–5 and Appendix C retain these original experimental results. Retention from v1 does not change their empirical status.

M1.justification: The dense and MoE architectures, training objectives and routing procedures in Sections 3–5 are unchanged. Studying alternative routing mechanisms is newly identified as future work, not an implemented method change.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same synthetic phone-book and shortest-path tasks, natural-language benchmarks and math benchmarks. The complete training-mixture descriptions are retained, moving from Appendix A to B.

E2.justification: The same dense Transformer and MoE model series participate in the corresponding main-text and appendix comparisons. The added related-work citations introduce no evaluated comparators.

E3.justification: Sections 4.1 and 5.1 retain the same model configurations, splits, optimization settings and evaluation metrics. The Figure 5 analysis still samples 6,319 training problems, comprising 5,000 MATH-like and 1,319 GSM8k-like examples.

E4.justification: The expert/width comparisons, math generalization-gap analysis in Figure 5 and fixed-perplexity comparison in Figure 6 are retained. No ablation, robustness test or supplementary analysis is added or removed.

E5.justification: Both versions present the same curves without error bars and report no experimental seed counts, repeated-run variability, confidence intervals or significance tests.

E6.justification: Figures 1 and 4–12 retain the same plotted results, comparator series and benchmark entries, including all appendix results. The prose revisions change interpretations rather than numerical values, rankings or empirical findings.

T1.justification: Section 3 retains the same definitions, assumptions, bounds and constructions. The proofs move from Appendix C to D with renumbered statements, without changes to mathematical reasoning.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and discussion retain the central claim that increasing experts benefits memorization and knowledge-intensive tasks more than reasoning, while width and active parameters remain important for reasoning.

C2.justification: Section 5 clarifies that memorization denotes factual recall, and Section 5.2 describes the math generalization gap as overfitting and revises the fixed-perplexity explanation around architectural implicit bias. New qualifications acknowledge tasks that are neither pure memorization nor pure reasoning and leave alternative routers untested. The existing model-scale limitation is retained.

D1.justification: The implementation codebases, hyperparameters, routing details and data-processing instructions are unchanged. The training-data appendix is renumbered, and code/data access information is retained.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds Nichani et al. (2024) on factual recall and Chen and Zou (2024) on transformer depth. It also removes the statement that MoE reasoning comparisons have received comparatively less attention, making a limited positioning revision.

P1.justification: Localized terminology and paragraph revisions accompany moving and expanding limitations into Appendix A, renumbering the existing appendices and updating the publication header. Renumbering leaves a stale reference to Lemma C.8 in Corollary D.9.

P2.justification: Figure 5's caption is shortened, and appendix headings and figures shift within the layout. The per-perplexity subsection heading now follows Figure 9. All twelve figures retain their graphic content; no displays are added or removed.

improvement.justification: Compared with v1, v2 more clearly identifies factual recall as the measured capability and acknowledges mixed-task and routing limitations in Section 5 and Appendix A. These changes modestly improve interpretation of the unchanged evidence. The gain is limited, with a small editing regression from the stale Lemma C.8 reference in Corollary D.9.
